summary:
Respected judges and everyone.

Our project is called AstroHealth, a Smart Astronaut Health Monitoring and Decision Support System.

Space exploration is one of humanity's greatest achievements. However, astronauts face several health challenges during space missions, including microgravity, radiation exposure, sleep disturbances, and isolation.

Our problem is that astronauts need to monitor multiple health indicators, but understanding unusual measurements and their significance can be challenging.

To address this problem, we propose AstroHealth.

Our system collects health measurements and displays them through a simple and interactive dashboard.

It monitors indicators such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep duration, and physical activity.

The unique feature of our project is its explanatory health-monitoring system. Instead of simply displaying numbers, AstroHealth explains what each measurement represents, why it matters, and what the astronaut should consider when a reading appears unusual.

The system also provides measurement reminders and can be adapted for different mission environments, including spacecraft, space stations, and lunar missions.

Our current prototype demonstrates the dashboard, simulated health measurements, alerts, and explanatory information.
In the future, we aim to integrate compatible wearable sensors, personalized health baselines, and relevant NASA .
details:
Our project is an astronaut health monitoring system that measures key health vitals such as body temperature, heart rate, blood oxygen levels, and sleep duration. Users can select different mission environments—such as a spacecraft, space station, or lunar surface—and the system automatically adjusts and displays health details tailored to that specific location.

This project helps astronauts track their health regularly and sends timely measurement reminders so no check-up is missed. Our intended impact is to improve the overall health and safety of astronauts, helping them stay fit, detect health issues early, and remain mission-ready during long space journeys.

To build this project, we used HTML and JavaScript for coding and Canva for designing our presentation. What makes our project creative is its ability to combine multi-environment space tracking with smart reminders in one simple, easy-to-use dashboard. While developing it, our team focused on user-friendly design, accuracy of health metrics, and the unique physical challenges astronauts face in different space environments.

Note on AI Usage: We used AI tools to gather additional information, fix coding errors, and improve our English grammar and sentence structure since English is not our first language.
